## Lessons from our previous project: tests and verification time (2026-11-10)
Source: two clean-up lots on Panthelia, our long-running Unreal project (UE 5.8, C++, about 7,300 automation tests), both closed on 2026-11-10. We carry over the rules, not the code. Each rule below cost us real hours once.

**What it cost.** In one week of November that project ran 1,333 headless test runs: 25.7 hours of machine time. 586 of those were mutation runs, each with two rebuilds. The pre-commit check took 334 s and the full suite about 15 minutes. After the two lots the same checks take about 90–105 s and about 6 minutes, with 37 pointless tests removed and everything else still green. None of the gain came from faster hardware.

### What to test in a 4-day jam
- **Test only logic that is easy to break and hard to see by playing:** scoring, save and load, state machines, generators, math. Everything else is verified by playing the packaged build.
- **Keep the whole suite under 30 seconds of test time.** A check that takes minutes stops being run.
- **Do not write tests that are not tests.** We deleted 37: scans of the source text, checks that a field exists, and copies of constants, colors and UI positions. They fail when someone edits a number, not when the game breaks.
- **No registers.** No test catalog, no list of "known failures", no exclusion list. A run is green or red, and a red test is fixed or deleted the same day. Our registers needed a full suite run just to be refreshed, and a stale one blocked the check before Unreal even started.
- **Read a test's body before deleting it; the name can lie.** Six of the 37 looked like layout checks by name and tested real behavior. Two reviewers caught it and we restored them.
- **Name tests by tier, and never let a test name also be a folder.** If `Game.Save.Validate` exists and someone adds `Game.Save.Validate.Slots`, Unreal's Automation tree keeps the folder and silently stops running the first test. We had one that had stopped running and nobody saw it, because a test that does not run does not fail.

### A test needs an oracle that can fail
- For every test, ask: **what wrong implementation would still pass this?** If the answer is "most of them", the test is decoration.
- **One check per fixture when state latches.** We checked two things in one session of a tool whose "write detected" flag stays set until the session ends. When the first check tripped it, the second passed for the wrong reason. Each check now runs in its own session.
- **Mutate by risk, not per test.** Break the code on purpose in 1 to 3 places per change (a wrong result, a skipped guard, an unwanted side effect) and confirm the matching test fails for the expected reason. Mutating every test was our largest single source of runs.

### Measure before optimizing
- **Get three numbers first:** Editor boot, the sum of the test durations, and the wall time. What is left over is overhead. In our 225 s check they were 37 s, 114 s and 225 s, and even the 114 s was inflated: each duration included a wait for the next Editor frame. The real work of the tests was about 45 s.
- **Measure the whole, not the part.** Booting without the startup map cut one test family from 273 s to 31 s, so it looked like a pure win. On the full check it was slower (254 s against 225 s) and one test failed, because other tests relied on what the map kept loaded.
- **Timings vary from run to run.** The same code measured between 87 s and 108 s. Compare two paths on the same tree and report a range, not the best run.

### Where the time really went
- **The engine's `Automation RunTests` path spends about 4.5 Editor frames on every test.** The controller and the worker talk through messages, and the worker closes each test on the next frame. A test that takes microseconds reported 9.4 ms. With a few dozen tests this does not matter; with thousands it was most of the run. If it ever matters: `FAutomationTestFramework::RunSmokeTests` shows the engine running tests back to back (`StartTestByName` then `StopTest`), and that is the pattern we followed.
  - Details that bit us when doing that: drive it from `FCoreDelegates::OnEndFrame`, not from `FTSTicker` (some tests tick the global ticker themselves); a test that queues latent commands must get a real engine frame before the first one runs; flush the logs written by other threads before closing a test; and stop the engine's Automation worker, because it also advances latent commands and can close your test first.
- **Editor boot is most of a small run.** Flags that helped a headless run: `-unattended -nopause -nosplash -NullRHI -nosound -nocrashreports`.
  - `-nocrashreports`: every ensure a test triggers on purpose spent 2–10 s preparing a crash report nobody reads (one test went from 13.6 s to 0.9 s).
  - The startup map: loading our test level cost 14 s of every boot. **Give the jam project a small, nearly empty Editor startup map**, not the gameplay level.
  - `bEnableUncontrolledChangelists=False` (`[/Script/SourceControl.SourceControlPreferences]`, Editor ini): it scanned all 26,000 assets at boot.
  - Join several test filters with `+` in one run, so boot is paid once.
  - Exit with a forced exit once the report is on disk: the Editor's orderly shutdown took about 5 s.
- **Filters match by substring unless anchored.** Start a filter with `^` and end it with a dot (`^Game.Save.`), or `Game.Save` also selects `Tools.Whatever.Game.SaveSlots`.

### Costs that grow with everything that is loaded
- **A tool operation must not cost in proportion to all loaded content.** One of our Editor tools hashed every loaded package on each call: 2.9 s per call, 741 s of a 1,031 s suite, and just as slow in real use. If a tool truly has to read everything, do it in parallel (`ParallelFor`) and keep the decision on the game thread. With that, and with the tools booting without the map, it went down to 158 s.
- **Do not key a cache on file size plus modification time.** Unreal returns file times with **one-second** precision on Windows, so two same-size writes within a second look identical. A reviewer caught this before it shipped.
- **Do not call `CollectGarbage(RF_NoFlags)` in a test.** It unloads every asset nothing references. The next test that needs the player content reloads it, about 12 s each time. Use `GARBAGE_COLLECTION_KEEPFLAGS`.
- **Watch how long the player Blueprint takes to load, from day one.** Ours takes about 12 s. We did not find out why; the log points at skinned meshes and motion-matching data loaded through hard references. Whatever a character Blueprint hard-references is loaded with it, every time it is needed. Use soft references for anything not needed at spawn.
- **A test loads what it needs and cleans up what it loads.** Tests that leaned on the startup map's leftovers, or that loaded a level and left it initialized, were the ones that broke when the environment changed.

### Verdicts and evidence
- **Decide pass or fail from the report, not only from the exit code.** Our runner cross-checks the list of tests it asked for against the list that actually ran, and refuses a run where they differ.
- **Guard against a silently small selection.** A typo in a filter, or a module that failed to load, gives a green run with half the tests. Require a minimum count.
- **Count error-level ensures in the log even when every test passes.** An ensure during module start-up fires before any test exists to see it.
- **Every run writes to its own new folder** with a small summary file. Never reuse a report folder.
- **When a suite fails and no code changed, compare the engine version in the two logs first.** Our engine updated itself from 5.8.3 to 5.8.4 overnight and broke four tests. For the jam: stay on 5.9.0 and do not let the launcher update it before submission.

### Working with agents and scripts
- **A second model reviews anything that guards data, and every finding is checked in the code before acting on it.** The one-second timestamp problem was missed by the author and by one reviewer, and found by the other.
- **One build or test run at a time per machine.** A build cannot link while an Editor process holds the DLLs, and a measurement taken during someone else's build is worthless.
- **Long commands run in the background and report when done.** No polling loops.
- **Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a `.ps1` without a BOM as ANSI.** Accented characters in the script turn into garbage; ours corrupted a source comment. Keep scripts ASCII or save them with a BOM.
- **`ValidateSet` ignores case, `-ceq` does not.** `-Mode direct` passed validation and then took the wrong branch. Normalize the value once.
- **In JavaScript, `text.replace(a, b)` expands `$` patterns inside `b`.** A replacement text that contained a dollar sign followed by a backtick pasted the whole preceding document into itself three times. Use `split(a).join(b)` or slices for literal replacements.
- **Put one-off scripts in a file, not inline in a shell command.** Nested quoting failed on us more than once in a single afternoon.

### The short version for the jam
1. A handful of tests on pure logic, under 30 s in total. Play the packaged build for everything else.
2. Green or red. No lists of exceptions.
3. Anchored filters, one boot per run, a nearly empty startup map.
4. Before optimizing anything, measure boot, test time and wall time.
5. No tool call or test may cost in proportion to everything that is loaded.
6. Stay on UE 5.9.0 until we submit.

**Kit change (2026-11-10):** the kit `CLAUDE.md` now has a "Tests y verificación" section with these rules (plus "every test must be able to fail" and the script traps), so every agent working on the jam project loads them without having to open this log.

## Open decisions (owner)
- Moving assets between machines: GitHub LFS (1 GB free quota) or a cloud folder.
- AI provider credits: Rodin, Unreal Canvas, ElevenLabs.
- Team name and members (each with their Epic email).

## Reminders
- The Claude Code sign-in on ASSETS expires between Nov 15 and 18: run `claude auth login` on Nov 11 or 12.
- After the jam: `Tools/Devlog/Install-DevlogHooks.ps1 -Uninstall` on each machine.
- Start the EmbeddingGemma server with `D:\Models\EmbeddingGemma-2\start_embedding_server.bat` (about 1.5 GB of VRAM).

<#
Package-Jam.ps1 - Empaqueta el juego para la entrega de la jam y arma el zip.
Receta probada en UE 5.9.0 (CL 60351404) el 2026-11-09:
  - UAT BuildCookRun Win64 Development con -build -cook -stage -pak -iostore -archive.
  - NO usar -nocompileeditor: con plugins no-default activos (p. ej. AllToolsets) el cook
    busca <Proyecto>Editor.target y falla si no se compilo.
  - Config/DefaultGame.ini con bUseZenStore=False (en la maquina de assets el cook murio
    escribiendo en la carpeta de Zen; causa no confirmada). El script lo comprueba.
  - El zip EXCLUYE los .pdb (simbolos de depuracion, ~340 MB que no hacen falta).
  - Limite de la jam: zip < 1 GB, nombre TeamName_GameName.zip.

Uso:
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Package-Jam.ps1 -Project D:\Jam\MiJuego\MiJuego.uproject -ZipName Equipo_Juego
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Project,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$ZipName,
    [string]$EngineDir = 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9',
    [string]$Config = 'Development'
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$projDir = Split-Path $Project -Parent
$buildDir = Join-Path $projDir 'Build'
$logFile = Join-Path $projDir 'Saved\uat_package.log'
[void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory((Split-Path $logFile -Parent))

$game = Join-Path $projDir 'Config\DefaultGame.ini'
$zenOff = (Test-Path $game) -and (Select-String $game -Pattern '^\s*bUseZenStore\s*=\s*False' -Quiet)
if (-not $zenOff) {
    Write-Host 'AVISO: falta bUseZenStore=False en Config/DefaultGame.ini. Se agrega.'
    [void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory((Split-Path $game -Parent))   # proyecto sin Config/ (2026-11-11)
    Add-Content $game "`r`n[/Script/UnrealEd.ProjectPackagingSettings]`r`nbUseZenStore=False`r`n"
}

$uat = Join-Path $EngineDir 'Engine\Build\BatchFiles\RunUAT.bat'
$uatArgs = @('BuildCookRun', "-project=`"$Project`"", '-platform=Win64', "-clientconfig=$Config",
          '-build', '-cook', '-stage', '-pak', '-iostore', '-archive', "-archivedirectory=`"$buildDir`"",
          '-noP4', '-utf8output', '-unattended')
Write-Host "UAT -> $logFile"
& cmd.exe /d /c "`"$uat`" $($uatArgs -join ' ') > `"$logFile`" 2>&1"
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
Get-Content $logFile -Tail 4
if ($code -ne 0) {
    Write-Host "FALLO UAT (exit $code). Primeras lineas de error:"
    Select-String $logFile -Pattern 'Error:|Exception|Cook failed' | Select-Object -First 15 | ForEach-Object Line
    exit $code
}

$win = Join-Path $buildDir 'Windows'
$zip = Join-Path $projDir "$ZipName.zip"
if (Test-Path $zip) { Remove-Item $zip -Force }
Remove-Item (Join-Path $win '*\Saved') -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
$z = [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::Open($zip, 'Create')
try {
    Get-ChildItem $win -Recurse -File | Where-Object { $_.Extension -ne '.pdb' } | ForEach-Object {
        [void][System.IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::CreateEntryFromFile($z, $_.FullName, $_.FullName.Substring($win.Length + 1), 'Optimal')
    }
} finally { $z.Dispose() }
$mb = [math]::Round((Get-Item $zip).Length / 1MB, 1)
Write-Host "ZIP: $zip ($mb MB)"
if ($mb -ge 1024) { Write-Host 'FALLO: el zip supera 1 GB (limite de la jam). Usar butler o recortar contenido.'; exit 2 }
exit 0

176	## Lessons from our previous project: tests and verification time (2026-11-10)
177	Source: two clean-up lots on Panthelia, our long-running Unreal project (UE 5.8, C++, about 7,300 automation tests), both closed on 2026-11-10. We carry over the rules, not the code. Each rule below cost us real hours once.
178	
179	**What it cost.** In one week of November that project ran 1,333 headless test runs: 25.7 hours of machine time. 586 of those were mutation runs, each with two rebuilds. The pre-commit check took 334 s and the full suite about 15 minutes. After the two lots the same checks take about 90–105 s and about 6 minutes, with 37 pointless tests removed and everything else still green. None of the gain came from faster hardware.
180	
181	### What to test in a 4-day jam
182	- **Test only logic that is easy to break and hard to see by playing:** scoring, save and load, state machines, generators, math. Everything else is verified by playing the packaged build.
183	- **Keep the whole suite under 30 seconds of test time.** A check that takes minutes stops being run.
184	- **Do not write tests that are not tests.** We deleted 37: scans of the source text, checks that a field exists, and copies of constants, colors and UI positions. They fail when someone edits a number, not when the game breaks.
185	- **No registers.** No test catalog, no list of "known failures", no exclusion list. A run is green or red, and a red test is fixed or deleted the same day. Our registers needed a full suite run just to be refreshed, and a stale one blocked the check before Unreal even started.
186	- **Read a test's body before deleting it; the name can lie.** Six of the 37 looked like layout checks by name and tested real behavior. Two reviewers caught it and we restored them.
187	- **Name tests by tier, and never let a test name also be a folder.** If `Game.Save.Validate` exists and someone adds `Game.Save.Validate.Slots`, Unreal's Automation tree keeps the folder and silently stops running the first test. We had one that had stopped running and nobody saw it, because a test that does not run does not fail.
188	
189	### A test needs an oracle that can fail
190	- For every test, ask: **what wrong implementation would still pass this?** If the answer is "most of them", the test is decoration.
191	- **One check per fixture when state latches.** We checked two things in one session of a tool whose "write detected" flag stays set until the session ends. When the first check tripped it, the second passed for the wrong reason. Each check now runs in its own session.
192	- **Mutate by risk, not per test.** Break the code on purpose in 1 to 3 places per change (a wrong result, a skipped guard, an unwanted side effect) and confirm the matching test fails for the expected reason. Mutating every test was our largest single source of runs.
193	
194	### Measure before optimizing
195	- **Get three numbers first:** Editor boot, the sum of the test durations, and the wall time. What is left over is overhead. In our 225 s check they were 37 s, 114 s and 225 s, and even the 114 s was inflated: each duration included a wait for the next Editor frame. The real work of the tests was about 45 s.
196	- **Measure the whole, not the part.** Booting without the startup map cut one test family from 273 s to 31 s, so it looked like a pure win. On the full check it was slower (254 s against 225 s) and one test failed, because other tests relied on what the map kept loaded.
197	- **Timings vary from run to run.** The same code measured between 87 s and 108 s. Compare two paths on the same tree and report a range, not the best run.
198	
199	### Where the time really went
200	- **The engine's `Automation RunTests` path spends about 4.5 Editor frames on every test.** The controller and the worker talk through messages, and the worker closes each test on the next frame. A test that takes microseconds reported 9.4 ms. With a few dozen tests this does not matter; with thousands it was most of the run. If it ever matters: `FAutomationTestFramework::RunSmokeTests` shows the engine running tests back to back (`StartTestByName` then `StopTest`), and that is the pattern we followed.
201	  - Details that bit us when doing that: drive it from `FCoreDelegates::OnEndFrame`, not from `FTSTicker` (some tests tick the global ticker themselves); a test that queues latent commands must get a real engine frame before the first one runs; flush the logs written by other threads before closing a test; and stop the engine's Automation worker, because it also advances latent commands and can close your test first.
202	- **Editor boot is most of a small run.** Flags that helped a headless run: `-unattended -nopause -nosplash -NullRHI -nosound -nocrashreports`.
203	  - `-nocrashreports`: every ensure a test triggers on purpose spent 2–10 s preparing a crash report nobody reads (one test went from 13.6 s to 0.9 s).
204	  - The startup map: loading our test level cost 14 s of every boot. **Give the jam project a small, nearly empty Editor startup map**, not the gameplay level.
205	  - `bEnableUncontrolledChangelists=False` (`[/Script/SourceControl.SourceControlPreferences]`, Editor ini): it scanned all 26,000 assets at boot.
206	  - Join several test filters with `+` in one run, so boot is paid once.
207	  - Exit with a forced exit once the report is on disk: the Editor's orderly shutdown took about 5 s.
208	- **Filters match by substring unless anchored.** Start a filter with `^` and end it with a dot (`^Game.Save.`), or `Game.Save` also selects `Tools.Whatever.Game.SaveSlots`.
209	
210	### Costs that grow with everything that is loaded
211	- **A tool operation must not cost in proportion to all loaded content.** One of our Editor tools hashed every loaded package on each call: 2.9 s per call, 741 s of a 1,031 s suite, and just as slow in real use. If a tool truly has to read everything, do it in parallel (`ParallelFor`) and keep the decision on the game thread. With that, and with the tools booting without the map, it went down to 158 s.
212	- **Do not key a cache on file size plus modification time.** Unreal returns file times with **one-second** precision on Windows, so two same-size writes within a second look identical. A reviewer caught this before it shipped.
213	- **Do not call `CollectGarbage(RF_NoFlags)` in a test.** It unloads every asset nothing references. The next test that needs the player content reloads it, about 12 s each time. Use `GARBAGE_COLLECTION_KEEPFLAGS`.
214	- **Watch how long the player Blueprint takes to load, from day one.** Ours takes about 12 s. We did not find out why; the log points at skinned meshes and motion-matching data loaded through hard references. Whatever a character Blueprint hard-references is loaded with it, every time it is needed. Use soft references for anything not needed at spawn.
215	- **A test loads what it needs and cleans up what it loads.** Tests that leaned on the startup map's leftovers, or that loaded a level and left it initialized, were the ones that broke when the environment changed.
216	
217	### Verdicts and evidence
218	- **Decide pass or fail from the report, not only from the exit code.** Our runner cross-checks the list of tests it asked for against the list that actually ran, and refuses a run where they differ.
219	- **Guard against a silently small selection.** A typo in a filter, or a module that failed to load, gives a green run with half the tests. Require a minimum count.
220	- **Count error-level ensures in the log even when every test passes.** An ensure during module start-up fires before any test exists to see it.
221	- **Every run writes to its own new folder** with a small summary file. Never reuse a report folder.
222	- **When a suite fails and no code changed, compare the engine version in the two logs first.** Our engine updated itself from 5.8.3 to 5.8.4 overnight and broke four tests. For the jam: stay on 5.9.0 and do not let the launcher update it before submission.
223	
224	### Working with agents and scripts
225	- **A second model reviews anything that guards data, and every finding is checked in the code before acting on it.** The one-second timestamp problem was missed by the author and by one reviewer, and found by the other.
226	- **One build or test run at a time per machine.** A build cannot link while an Editor process holds the DLLs, and a measurement taken during someone else's build is worthless.
227	- **Long commands run in the background and report when done.** No polling loops.
228	- **Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a `.ps1` without a BOM as ANSI.** Accented characters in the script turn into garbage; ours corrupted a source comment. Keep scripts ASCII or save them with a BOM.
229	- **`ValidateSet` ignores case, `-ceq` does not.** `-Mode direct` passed validation and then took the wrong branch. Normalize the value once.
230	- **In JavaScript, `text.replace(a, b)` expands `$` patterns inside `b`.** A replacement text that contained a dollar sign followed by a backtick pasted the whole preceding document into itself three times. Use `split(a).join(b)` or slices for literal replacements.
231	- **Put one-off scripts in a file, not inline in a shell command.** Nested quoting failed on us more than once in a single afternoon.
232	
233	### The short version for the jam
234	1. A handful of tests on pure logic, under 30 s in total. Play the packaged build for everything else.
235	2. Green or red. No lists of exceptions.
236	3. Anchored filters, one boot per run, a nearly empty startup map.
237	4. Before optimizing anything, measure boot, test time and wall time.
238	5. No tool call or test may cost in proportion to everything that is loaded.
239	6. Stay on UE 5.9.0 until we submit.
240	
241	**Kit change (2026-11-10):** the kit `CLAUDE.md` now has a "Tests y verificación" section with these rules (plus "every test must be able to fail" and the script traps), so every agent working on the jam project loads them without having to open this log.

Sí, lo entiendo todo y no hay nada que me bloquee. Leí `CLAUDE.md`, `Devlog/README.md`, el GDD v0.12 completo, las lecciones de tests y los scripts de `Tools/`. Como me pediste avisar antes, no he tocado nada todavía.

## Plan de hoy

1. **Proyecto:** `C:\GameJam\Glyphbound\` en C++ desde la plantilla en blanco (no la de primera persona de Epic), con los plugins no usados apagados y el arranque del Editor medido antes y después.
2. **Jugador:** moverse, saltar, doble salto y dash, con vida y maná que regeneran y las teclas del GDD §9.
3. **Combate:** bastón con ataque básico, pistola y cambio entre ambos; Fireball con todos sus parámetros en datos y dos entradas de 0 a 1 (potencia y alcance) que mañana alimenta el QTE.
4. **Eras:** un mapa de prueba con portal y fundido que alterna pasado y futuro; manos en pixel art generadas como placeholder.
5. **Cierre:** tests solo de lógica pura, empaquetar `TeamTBD_Glyphbound`, `New-DevlogDay.ps1` y `Design/HANDOFF.md`.

## Lo que doy por hecho (corrígeme si no)

- **Git no guarda `Content/`** (decisión del equipo en `.gitignore`). Pondré en código y archivos de texto todo lo que pueda, para que quede en el historial. Lo que sea asset binario (el mapa, por ejemplo) vivirá solo en CENTRAL.
- **Arrancar el `.exe` empaquetado para comprobar que carga y cierra** no cuenta como PIE, así que lo haré yo. Jugarlo de verdad te lo pido a ti.
- **La estructura base del proyecto la escribo yo directamente** (`.uproject`, módulos, configuración) y lo anoto como excepción en la bitácora. Los sistemas de juego van a Muse Spark por `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`.
- **El primer commit incluye lo pendiente:** el cambio sin confirmar de `Devlog/PREJAM_PREP.md` y `Devlog/raw/`.
- **DLSS no entra hoy.** El plugin no está instalado en el motor; lo reviso el día 2 y te pediré permiso antes de descargar nada.

## Una pregunta que no bloquea

La tarea de copia diaria `JamContentBackup` sigue desactivada y apunta a una carpeta de ejemplo. Como `Content/` no va a git, esa copia es el único respaldo del mapa y los assets. ¿La activas tú cuando exista el proyecto, o la edito y activo yo?

Aún no he comprobado que Muse Spark responda por OpenCode (está instalado, v2.2.7); será lo primero que pruebe al delegar.

---
name: jam-autonomy-and-agent-routing
description: Glyphbound jam - never stop to ask; how to route work between Muse Spark, Claude subagents and Codex Sol 6.1
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Owner instructions given 2026-11-12 (Epic AI MegaJam, project Glyphbound), in their words summarized:

- **Do not stop to ask for authorizations, go-aheads or yes/no questions.** The owner is often away for hours; if the architect stops, the whole project stops. Find a simple solution and keep working.
- **Serial work (one code batch at a time) goes to Muse Spark via OpenCode.** Only one OpenCode session at a time.
- **When several subagents would genuinely speed things up, use Claude subagents (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) in parallel instead of Muse Spark.** Never above effort High for any of them.
- **Codex CLI with Sol 6.1 at Medium** is the second opinion and the reviewer for important code reviews.
- Priority early on: code structure for the whole game, not looks. Spells must be modular with every parameter adjustable. Keep it "a first-person RPG shooter that does not want to be too complicated". GAS or not is the architect's call.
- The content backup task (JamContentBackup) was explicitly left off for now.

**Why:** time is the scarce resource in a 4-day jam and nobody on the team is a programmer.
**How to apply:** take technical decisions alone, log them in the devlog, and only surface things at the end of a block. See [[implementer-muse-spark-opencode]] and [[commit-changes-always]].

<#
Build-Jam.ps1 - Compiles the Glyphbound C++ module (Editor target by default) and prints only what matters.
One build at a time per machine: do not run this while another build, a package or a test run is going.
The Editor must be closed (a full build cannot link while the Editor holds the DLLs).

Usage:
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1                 # GlyphboundEditor Win64 Development
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1 -Target Glyphbound   # game target

Output: full log in Glyphbound/Saved/Logs/build_last.log; the console shows errors (first 60) and the result line.
Exit code: 0 = Result: Succeeded.
#>
param(
    [string]$Project = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\..\Glyphbound\Glyphbound.uproject'),
    [string]$Target = 'GlyphboundEditor',
    [string]$Config = 'Development',
    [string]$EngineDir = 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9',
    [int]$MaxErrors = 60
)
$Project = (Resolve-Path $Project).Path
$projDir = Split-Path $Project -Parent
$logDir = Join-Path $projDir 'Saved\Logs'
[void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($logDir)
$log = Join-Path $logDir 'build_last.log'
$bat = Join-Path $EngineDir 'Engine\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat'
$sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
& cmd.exe /d /c "`"$bat`" $Target Win64 $Config -project=`"$Project`" -waitmutex > `"$log`" 2>&1"
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
$sw.Stop()
$errors = Select-String -Path $log -Pattern '(: error |: fatal error |error LNK|Error: |ERROR: |UHT.*[Ee]rror)' | Select-Object -First $MaxErrors
if ($errors) { $errors | ForEach-Object { $_.Line.Trim() } }
$result = Select-String -Path $log -Pattern '^Result: ' | Select-Object -Last 1
if ($result) { Write-Host $result.Line } else { Write-Host "No 'Result:' line found (exit $code). See $log" }
Write-Host ("Build time: {0:N0} s  (exit {1})  log: {2}" -f $sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, $code, $log)
exit $code

<#
Stop-EditorMcp.ps1 - Cierra el Editor de forma ordenada por MCP (consola: QUIT_EDITOR).
Cerrar la ventana a mano/CloseMainWindow no basta en 5.9 (queda colgado). Nunca matar el proceso.
ANTES: guardar el trabajo. QUIT_EDITOR puede mostrar el dialogo de guardar si hay cambios.
Uso:  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Stop-EditorMcp.ps1 -Port 8059
#>
param([int]$Port = 8059, [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 120)
$u = "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/mcp"
$h = @{ 'Accept' = 'application/json, text/event-stream' }
$init = @{ jsonrpc = '2.0'; id = 1; method = 'initialize'; params = @{ protocolVersion = '2025-06-18'; capabilities = @{}; clientInfo = @{ name = 'jam-stop'; version = '1' } } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 -Compress
$r = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $u -Method Post -Headers $h -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $init -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 20
$initTxt = if ($r.Content -is [byte[]]) { [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString($r.Content) } else { [string]$r.Content }
$meta = ($initTxt | ConvertFrom-Json).result._meta.'com.epicgames.unrealengine/instance'
$pid0 = $meta.processId
$projDir = $meta.projectDirectory
$h['Mcp-Session-Id'] = $r.Headers['Mcp-Session-Id']
# Cerrar primero los editores de assets abiertos: con el editor de animacion (Persona) abierto,
# QUIT_EDITOR crasheo al apagar (EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION en UnrealEditor-Persona, 2026-11-10).
function Invoke-EdTool($tool, $toolArgs) {
    $b = @{ jsonrpc = '2.0'; id = 3; method = 'tools/call'; params = @{ name = 'call_tool'; arguments = @{ toolset_name = 'EditorToolset.EditorAppToolset'; tool_name = $tool; arguments = $toolArgs } } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8 -Compress
    $x = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $u -Method Post -Headers $h -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $b -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 30
    $s = if ($x.Content -is [byte[]]) { [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString($x.Content) } else { [string]$x.Content }
    if ($s -match '^\s*(event:|data:)') { $s = (($s -split "`n") | Where-Object { $_ -like 'data:*' } | ForEach-Object { $_.Substring(5) }) -join '' }
    return ($s | ConvertFrom-Json)
}
try {
    $open = @((Invoke-EdTool 'GetOpenAssets' @{}).result.structuredContent.returnValue)
    foreach ($a in $open) {
        $p = if ($a -is [string]) { $a } elseif ($a.refPath) { $a.refPath } elseif ($a.objectPath) { $a.objectPath } else { [string]$a }
        if ($p) {
            # unsavedChanges es obligatorio (Fail/Save/Discard); sin el, la tool falla y el editor sigue abierto.
            $c = Invoke-EdTool 'CloseEditorForAsset' @{ assetPath = $p; unsavedChanges = 'Save' }
            if ($c.result.isError) { Write-Host "AVISO: no se pudo cerrar el editor de $p : $($c.result.content[0].text)" } else { Write-Host "Cerrado editor de asset: $p" }
        }
    }
    # CloseEditorForAsset vuelve antes de que la ventana se destruya; si QUIT_EDITOR llega en ese
    # momento, Persona crashea igual (2026-11-10, segunda prueba). Esperar a que no quede ninguno.
    if ($open.Count -gt 0) {
        $limit2 = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(20)
        while ((Get-Date) -lt $limit2 -and @((Invoke-EdTool 'GetOpenAssets' @{}).result.structuredContent.returnValue).Count -gt 0) { Start-Sleep 1 }

<#
Measure-EditorBoot.ps1 - Boots the Editor N times (Start-EditorMcp / Stop-EditorMcp) and reports
"Total Editor Startup Time" from the log plus the number of mounted plugins.
Timings vary from run to run: report the range, not the best run (Devlog/PREJAM_PREP.md).

Usage: powershell -File Tools/Jam/Measure-EditorBoot.ps1 -Label baseline -Runs 2
Appends one line per run to Glyphbound/Saved/Logs/boot_measurements.csv
#>
param(
    [string]$Project = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\..\Glyphbound\Glyphbound.uproject'),
    [string]$Label = 'run',
    [int]$Runs = 2,
    [int]$Port = 8059
)
$Project = (Resolve-Path $Project).Path
$projDir = Split-Path $Project -Parent
$name = [IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($Project)
$log = Join-Path $projDir "Saved\Logs\$name.log"
$csv = Join-Path $projDir 'Saved\Logs\boot_measurements.csv'
if (-not (Test-Path $csv)) { 'utc,label,run,startup_seconds,mounted_plugins,mcp_ready' | Set-Content -Path $csv -Encoding ascii }
for ($i = 1; $i -le $Runs; $i++) {
    $out = & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Start-EditorMcp.ps1') -Project $Project -Port $Port
    $startCode = $LASTEXITCODE
    $ready = ($out | Select-String 'MCP listo en (\d+) s' | Select-Object -Last 1)
    $readyS = if ($ready) { $ready.Matches[0].Groups[1].Value } else { '' }
    # The startup line is written a moment after the MCP server starts: wait for it.
    $secs = ''
    for ($w = 0; $w -lt 30 -and -not $secs; $w++) {
        $m = Select-String -Path $log -Pattern 'Total Editor Startup Time, took ([\d\.]+)' | Select-Object -Last 1
        if ($m) { $secs = $m.Matches[0].Groups[1].Value } else { Start-Sleep 2 }
    }
    $mounted = @(Select-String -Path $log -Pattern 'Mounting (Engine|Project) plugin').Count
    Write-Host "[$Label] run ${i}: startup=$secs s, mounted plugins=$mounted, MCP ready=$readyS s (start exit $startCode)"
    ('{0},{1},{2},{3},{4},{5}' -f [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('o'), $Label, $i, $secs, $mounted, $readyS) | Add-Content -Path $csv -Encoding ascii
    & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Stop-EditorMcp.ps1') -Port $Port | Select-Object -Last 2
    Start-Sleep 3
}

12	 *

14	 *   AGBSpell_Projectile  fireball, lightning bolt      (launches an AGBProjectile)
15	 *   AGBSpell_Wall        fire wall, ice wall           (a wall in front of the caster; blocks and/or burns)
16	 *   AGBSpell_Zone        ice floor                     (ground area that applies an effect / damage over time)
17	 *   AGBSpell_Trap        lightning rune                (arms on the ground, triggers when an enemy steps on it)
18	 *   AGBSpell_Orb         static-electricity ball       (moves forward and damages everything around it)
19	 *   AGBSpell_Beam        flamethrower                  (sustained cone from the caster's aim)

27	{
28		GENERATED_BODY()
29	
30	public:
31		AGBSpellActor();
32	
33		/** Called once, right after spawn. Subclasses call Super first (it stores SpellCast). */
34		virtual void InitSpell(const FGBSpellCast& InCast);
35	
36		/** Sustained spells: the cast input was pressed again, the caster switched weapon, or died. Default: EndSpell(). */
37		virtual void OnCastReleased();
38	
39		/** True while a sustained spell is running (the spellbook keeps a reference and blocks other casts). */
40		virtual bool IsSustaining() const { return false; }
41	
42		const FGBSpellCast& GetSpellCast() const { return SpellCast; }
43		AActor* GetCaster() const { return SpellCast.Caster; }
44	
45		/** Fired once when the spell is over, just before the actor is destroyed. */
46		FSimpleMulticastDelegate OnSpellEnded;
47	
48	protected:
49		/** Broadcasts OnSpellEnded and destroys the actor. Safe to call twice. */
50		virtual void EndSpell();
51	
52		/** Finds the ground under a point (line trace down, world static). False if nothing within MaxDistance. */

56

58		UPROPERTY() FGBSpellCast SpellCast;
59		bool bEnded = false;
60	};

# Glyphbound: code architecture

> Written by the architect (Claude Code) on 2026-11-12. Source of truth for how the C++ is organized.
> Design lives in `Design/GDD.md`; this file says how the code implements it. Keep it short and current.

## Principles
1. **Data, not code.** Every gameplay number lives in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` and is read through `UGBDataSubsystem`. Code never hardcodes damage, costs, speeds, durations, sizes or timings. The JSON ships as loose files, so numbers can be tuned in a packaged build with a text editor (`gb.ReloadData` reloads while playing).
2. **One stat system.** A number is a *named stat*: base value from data, then modifiers. `UGBStatsComponent` evaluates `(Base + adds) * multipliers` (or an override). Skill-tree nodes, armor, status effects, air passives and the weapon enchant are all just groups of modifiers with a source name. Nothing else changes numbers.

4. **Spells are data + a behavior.** A spell is a `FGBSpellDefinition` (params with `Base/Min/Max/ScaledBy`) plus the class of an `AGBSpellActor` behavior. The QTE result (power, reach) scales the params tagged for it. A new spell that fits an existing behavior is a JSON entry, no code.

6. **Text in git.** No binary assets are required to run: input actions, the test arena, placeholder shapes and placeholder pixel sprites are all built in C++ from text. `Content/` is ignored by git except `Content/Data/`.

| `Weapons/` | Held items and slots | `UGBEquipmentComponent`, `AGBHeldItem`, `AGBStaff`, `AGBGun`, `AGBSword` |
| `Spells/` | Spellbook, cast resolution, behaviors | `UGBSpellbookComponent`, `FGBSpellCast`, `AGBSpellActor`, `AGBSpell_*` |
| `QTE/` | Quick-time event | `FGBQTESession`, `FGBGestureRecognizer`, `UGBQTEComponent` |
| `World/` | Eras, progress, interactables, test arena | `UGBEraSubsystem`, `UGBEraComponent`, `UGBProgressSubsystem`, `IGBInteractable`, `AGBPortal`, `AGBChest`, `AGBPickup`, `AGBCheckpointVolume`, `AGBTestArena` |

# Rules for every implementer on Glyphbound (read first)

You implement one part of **Glyphbound**, a first-person RPG shooter for the Epic AI MegaJam 2026, in **Unreal Engine 5.9.0**, C++. The architect (another agent) wrote the public headers; you write the implementation. Several implementers work **at the same time** on different folders, so the rules about file ownership matter.

## Read before writing
1. `C:\GameJam\Design\ARCHITECTURE.md` (the whole file, it is short).
2. `C:\GameJam\Design\GDD.md`: the sections named in your task.
3. In `C:\GameJam\Glyphbound\Source\Glyphbound\`: `Core/GBTypes.h`, `Core/GBStatNames.h`, `Core/GBPlaceholder.h`, `Data/GBDataTypes.h`, `Data/GBDataSubsystem.h`, `Stats/GBStatsComponent.h`, `Stats/GBAttributeComponent.h`, `Combat/GBCombatLibrary.h`, plus every header your task names. The header comments are the specification: implement what they say.

## File ownership
- You own ONLY the files listed in your task. Create the `.cpp` for each header you own, and new files inside your folders if you need them.
- **Never edit a file you do not own.** If you need something from another module that its header does not offer, code against what exists, and write the request in your final report.
- In headers you own you MAY add includes, private/protected members, helper methods and extra public methods. You MUST NOT remove, rename or change the signature of anything already public there: other implementers are calling it right now.
- Do not edit `Glyphbound.Build.cs`, `.uproject`, or `Config/`. Module dependencies available: Core, CoreUObject, Engine, InputCore, EnhancedInput, Json, JsonUtilities, AIModule, NavigationSystem, Slate, SlateCore, UMG. If you need another one, say so in your report.

## Hard rules
- **Do not build, do not run the Editor, do not run tests, do not commit, do not launch other agents.** The architect integrates and builds after everyone finishes. Write code that compiles: check every engine API you are not sure about in the engine source at `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9\Engine\Source` (grep the header). UE 5.9 is newer than your training data; when in doubt, look.
- **No gameplay numbers in code.** Damage, costs, cooldowns, speeds, sizes, durations, timings and counts come from the JSON data through `UGBDataSubsystem` and `UGBStatsComponent` (stat names in `Core/GBStatNames.h`). If you need a number that has no stat yet, add a named constant `inline const FName` in a header YOU own (same style as `GBStatNames.h`), read it from the data with a sensible default, put its value in your JSON file, and list it in your report. Layout pixels and pure visual offsets may be code constants.
- Everything must work when a JSON entry is missing: use the default argument, log a warning with `UE_LOG(LogGB, Warning, ...)`, never crash, never divide by zero.
- No binary assets. 3D placeholders: `GBPlaceholder::SetupShape` (engine basic shapes). Pixel-art placeholders: `UGBPixelSpriteLibrary` (sprites described as text in `Sprites.json`). Art rule (GDD 3): medieval and magic things are pixel-art sprites; cyberpunk things are 3D.
- No custom collision channels or profiles that need config: use the engine's default channels and filter by team in code (`UGBCombatLibrary::AreHostile`).
- Do not keep pointers to definitions (`FGBSpellDefinition*`...) across frames; keep the id.
- A class member must never be named `Cast` (it hides the engine's `Cast<T>()`).
- All on-screen text in English. Comments in English, and only where they explain a decision or a non-obvious rule. ASCII only.
- Includes are relative to the module root: `#include "Stats/GBStatsComponent.h"`. Every `.cpp` includes its own header first. Every header with reflected types includes its `.generated.h` last.
- Keep it simple. This is a 4-day jam: clear, short code that works beats clever code. No speculative abstractions beyond what the headers define.

## Tests (only if your task asks for them)
- Pure logic only, no world, no assets: `IMPLEMENT_SIMPLE_AUTOMATION_TEST(FName, "Glyphbound.<Area>.<Name>", EAutomationTestFlags::EditorContext | EAutomationTestFlags::EngineFilter)` inside `#if WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS`, in `Tests/GB<Area>Tests.cpp`.
- Each test must be able to fail: before writing it, ask which wrong implementation would still pass it. No tests that copy a constant, check that a field exists, or read source text.
- A test name must never be a prefix of another test name (`A.B` next to `A.B.C` silently stops `A.B`).
- Keep them few and fast (the whole suite must stay well under 30 s).

## Final report (your last message, plain text, short)
1. Files you wrote or changed.
2. Anything in your headers that you added to the public API.
3. Requests for other modules (what you needed and did not find).
4. Design values you had to invent (they will be marked provisional in the GDD).
5. Risks: API calls you could not verify, things you expect may not compile, behavior you are unsure about.

# Day 1: 2026-11-12

> Architect's entry, written by the AI architect (Claude Code) as the day went. A person on the team reviews it and adds the human side (play-test notes, screenshots) starting from `2026-11-12_DRAFT.md`.

## Summary in 3 lines
- The owner directed, the AI architect decided every technical point alone and built the project "Glyphbound" from an empty folder: UE 5.9.0, C++, no template gameplay code.
- The whole code structure of the game was laid out in one pass: the architect wrote the header contracts, then ten AI implementers filled them in parallel, and one integration pass made it build.
- TODO at close: result of the build, tests, package and the first human play-test.

## Goal of the day vs. result
| Goal | Result | Evidence (commit, screenshot, clip) |
|---|---|---|
| Create the UE 5.9.0 project with unused plugins off, measure Editor boot before and after | Done. See "Numbers" below | commit `8034a7c` |
| First-person controller (move, jump, double jump, dash) | TODO | |
| Pixel-art hands (placeholder) | TODO | |
| Staff with basic magic attack + a gun, with switching | TODO | |
| One spell, 100% data-driven, ready to scale with the QTE | TODO | |
| Health and mana with regeneration | TODO | |
| A portal that swaps past and future with a fade, in a test map | TODO | |
| Packaged build | TODO | |

## How we used AI today
| Agent / tool | Model | What for | Result | Log |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code (architect) | Claude Fable 5.2 | Read the GDD, took the technical decisions, created the project, wrote every public header (the contracts), split the work, integrated | TODO | `raw/CENTRAL/2026-11-12/claude-…` |
| Claude Code subagents | Claude Opus 5.5 (effort High) | Ten implementers in parallel, one per code folder, each filling the architect's headers | TODO | same session log |
| OpenCode | Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor (High) | Serial work: the integration build-and-fix pass | TODO | `raw/CENTRAL/2026-11-12/agents/…` |
| Codex CLI | GPT Sol 6.1 (Medium) | Second opinion: code review of the combat core | TODO | `raw/CENTRAL/2026-11-12/agents/…` |

**Prompt of the day** (the owner's kickoff instruction to the architect, written in Spanish; English translation below):
```
Tu autonomía: nadie del equipo es programador. Todas las decisiones técnicas y de ingeniería las tomas tú, sin
preguntarme [...] Quiero que hagas one shot de toda la base del proyecto. Los hechizos tienen que ser modulares y
tienen que poder ajustarse todos sus parámetros. [...] Y la codebase es literalmente tuya. Es tu responsabilidad
que quede lo mejor posible y tú eres el dueño de todas las decisiones sobre el código.
```
> "Your autonomy: nobody on the team is a programmer. You take every technical and engineering decision, without asking me [...] I want you to one-shot the whole base of the project. Spells must be modular and every one of their parameters must be adjustable. [...] And the codebase is literally yours. It is your responsibility to make it as good as possible, and you own every decision about the code."

This is the theme (DIRECTOR'S CUT) applied to the process: the owner sets the vision and the rules, and the AI directs the other AIs.

**What the AI did well:** TODO

**Where the AI failed and how we fixed it** (the part judges value most in a dev log): TODO

## Design decisions
All taken by the architect; the owner asked not to be consulted on engineering.

- **C++ only, built from the blank template.** The first-person template was not used: the jam asks for gameplay beyond Epic's templates, and AI agents handle C++ text far better than Blueprint graphs.
- **No Gameplay Ability System.** Considered (the GDD lists it as a candidate) and rejected: heavy boilerplate and asset setup for a 4-day jam. Replaced by three small pieces we fully control: one stat system (base value from data + stacked modifiers), one damage function, one status-effect component. Skill-tree nodes, armor, slows, potions, air passives and the weapon enchant are all "a named group of modifiers".
- **All gameplay numbers in JSON under `Content/Data`, shipped as loose files.** Reasons: git only carries text in this team (binary assets travel by a shared folder), AI agents edit text reliably, and the owner can retune a packaged build with a text editor and no Editor. `gb.ReloadData` reloads while playing. The GDD suggested data tables; JSON gives the same thing without binary assets.
- **Spells = data + a behavior class.** Each parameter has `Base / Min / Max / ScaledBy` (none, QTE power, QTE reach). Eight behaviors cover the nine active spells and the enchant; a new spell that fits a behavior is one JSON entry.
- **No binary assets needed to run.** The test arena, input actions and placeholders are built in C++; placeholder pixel art is ASCII rows in `Sprites.json` turned into textures at runtime. The default map is the engine's empty map, so the Editor boots on an empty level and the whole game is reviewable as text in git.
- **HUD drawn with the canvas, not widgets.** Two skins (90s RPG, cyberpunk) are two style structs. No widget assets to author by hand.
- **Contracts first, then parallel implementers.** The architect wrote every public header with the specification in comments, checked that they pass Unreal's header tool, and only then started ten implementers, each owning one folder and forbidden to touch the others. Reason: parallel agents drift apart unless the interfaces are fixed first.
- **Plugins:** the `AllToolsets` aggregator was replaced by the 18 Editor toolsets we use, and 103 default plugins were turned off by a script that checks every plugin dependency first (`Tools/Jam/trim_plugins.js`).

## Assets created
| Asset | Tool (AI or manual) | Prompt or source | License | Machine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Placeholder pixel sprites (`Content/Data/Sprites.json`, ASCII rows) | AI (Claude Opus 5.5 subagent) | Architect's task brief | Own work | CENTRAL |

No third-party assets today. Engine content used: basic shapes and engine materials that ship with UE 5.9.

## Problems and solutions
- **Trimming plugins did not speed up a warm Editor boot.** We expected a gain; measured, there is none worth the name (see Numbers). Mounted plugins went from 315 to 160, but warm boot stayed around 10-11 s. The cost of a warm boot is not in the plugin count. We keep the trimmed list anyway (fewer modules to load and cook, smaller package), and we did not spend more time on it. Lesson from the previous project confirmed: measure the whole thing before believing an optimization.

input.prompt:
You are implementer "FOUNDATION" on the Unreal Engine 5.9 C++ game Glyphbound. First read `C:\GameJam\Prompts\implementer_rules.md` and follow it exactly (it tells you what else to read). GDD sections for you: 0.1, 5, 6, 7 ("Requirements for the architect").

## Your files (you own only these; all under C:\GameJam\Glyphbound\)
- `Source/Glyphbound/Glyphbound.cpp` (already has IMPLEMENT_PRIMARY_GAME_MODULE; add `DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY(LogGB);` and the console commands below)
- `Source/Glyphbound/Data/GBDataTypes.cpp` (new: `FGBScaledParam::Resolve`)
- `Source/Glyphbound/Data/GBDataSubsystem.cpp` (new) for `Data/GBDataSubsystem.h`
- `Source/Glyphbound/Stats/GBStatsComponent.cpp`, `Stats/GBAttributeComponent.cpp` (new)
- `Source/Glyphbound/Core/GBPlaceholder.cpp` (new) for `Core/GBPlaceholder.h`
- `Source/Glyphbound/World/GBProgressSubsystem.cpp` (new) for `World/GBProgressSubsystem.h`
- `Source/Glyphbound/Tests/GBStatsTests.cpp` (new)
- `Content/Data/StatusEffects.json` (new)

## What to build
1. **UGBDataSubsystem**: load every file listed in the header comment from `FPaths::ProjectContentDir()/Data/` with `FFileHelper::LoadFileToString` + `FJsonSerializer` + `FJsonObjectConverter::JsonObjectToUStruct` / `JsonArrayToUStruct` (check their exact signatures in `Engine/Source/Runtime/JsonUtilities/Public/JsonObjectConverter.h`). Write ONE small generic helper for "load array field X of file F into TArray<T>" and one for "load whole file into struct T" and reuse them. Missing file or parse error: `UE_LOG(LogGB, Error, ...)` naming the file and the JSON error, plus an on-screen debug message in non-shipping builds, table left empty, no crash. Warn about duplicate ids and entries with an empty Id. `Find*` do a lookup through a TMap<FName,int32> index rebuilt on load (add the index maps as private members). `ReloadAll` re-reads everything, then broadcasts `OnDataReloaded`. `ParseColor` accepts "#RRGGBB" and "#RRGGBBAA" (sRGB hex to FLinearColor). `Get` returns the subsystem from the world's game instance (null-safe).
   - Console commands in `Glyphbound.cpp` using `FAutoConsoleCommandWithWorld` (or the WithWorldAndArgs variant): `gb.ReloadData` (calls ReloadAll on that world's game instance).
   - JSON keys must match the struct field names in `Data/GBDataTypes.h` (FJsonObjectConverter is case-insensitive on names; enums are written as their names, e.g. "Fire"; bools named `bEnabled` are written "bEnabled").
2. **FGBScaledParam::Resolve** per its header comment.
3. **UGBStatsComponent** per the header. `ApplyModifiers`: result = (Base + sum of Add) * product of Multiply; if any Override exists, the LAST Override wins and replaces the whole result. `Evaluate`/`EvaluateKeys` collect the active modifiers whose `Stat` equals one of the keys, in insertion order. `AddModifiers(Source, ...)` first removes that source, then adds each modifier with `Value` scaled by `ValueScale` this way: Add -> Value*Scale; Multiply -> 1 + (Value-1)*Scale; Override -> unchanged. Broadcast `OnStatsChanged` on any change. No tick.
4. **UGBAttributeComponent** per the header. Ticks to regenerate using `StepRegen` (no regen while dead; regen only after the delay since the last loss; clamp to max). When max health/mana drop below current values (stats changed), clamp. `ApplyDamage`: ignore if dead, invulnerable or Amount <= 0; copy the info, broadcast `OnModifyIncomingDamage(copy)`, multiply by the owner's `DamageTaken` stat (default 1), clamp to >= 0, subtract, broadcast `OnHealthChanged`, `OnDamaged(copy, actual)`, and on reaching 0 set dead and broadcast `OnDeath` once. `RestoreAll` revives. Bind to the owner's `UGBStatsComponent::OnStatsChanged` in BeginPlay to re-clamp and re-broadcast.
5. **GBPlaceholder** per the header. Meshes: `/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube.Cube`, `Sphere.Sphere`, `Cylinder.Cylinder`, `Cone.Cone`, `Plane.Plane` (all 100 cm). Materials: lit = `/Engine/BasicShapes/BasicShapeMaterial.BasicShapeMaterial` (vector parameter "Color"), glow = `/Engine/EngineMaterials/EmissiveMeshMaterial.EmissiveMeshMaterial` (vector parameter "Color", unlit additive). Load with `LoadObject` and cache in `TWeakObjectPtr` statics. `SetupShape` sets relative scale = SizeCm / 100, creates a `UMaterialInstanceDynamic` on slot 0 and sets "Color". `ElementColor(uint8)`: cast to `EGBElement` (Physical grey, Arcane violet, Fire orange, Lightning yellow, Ice cyan, Air pale green).
6. **UGBProgressSubsystem** per the header. `SaveCheckpoint` calls `AGBPlayerCharacter::SaveToSnapshot` and sets bValid; `RestoreCheckpoint` calls `LoadFromSnapshot` (the player header is `Player/GBPlayerCharacter.h`; you only call those two methods). Broadcast the delegates.
7. **StatusEffects.json**: `{ "StatusEffects": [ ... ] }` with these ids and provisional values: `Burn` (fire damage over time, 4 s, tick 0.5 s), `Shock` (short lightning effect: brief MoveSpeed x0.6 for 1.5 s), `Slow` (MoveSpeed x0.5, 4 s), `Chill` (MoveSpeed x0.7, 3 s), `HealthPotion` (heals over time: 10 s, tick 1 s, total about 60), `ManaPotion` (same idea for mana), `HealthInjection` (instant heal, smaller than the potion total, Duration 0), `Enchant_Fire`, `Enchant_Lightning`, `Enchant_Ice` (Duration 20 s; Modifiers on "Weapon.All.Damage" Multiply ~1.25; Strings: "WeaponElement": "Fire"/"Lightning"/"Ice" and "WeaponOnHitEffect": "Burn"/"Shock"/"Chill" - the gun code reads these two strings). Negative HealthPerTick = damage.
8. **Tests** (`Tests/GBStatsTests.cpp`), pure logic only, a handful: modifier order (add then multiply; last override wins; scaling of Multiply modifiers around 1), `StepRegen` (no regen before the delay, clamps at max, no regen at 0 rate), `FGBScaledParam::Resolve` (QTE off returns Base; Power-tagged ignores Reach; clamps scores to 0..1). Test names like `Glyphbound.Stats.ModifierOrder`.

Finish with the final report described in the rules file.

- `Source/Glyphbound/Tests/GBStatsTests.cpp` (new)
- `Content/Data/StatusEffects.json` (new)

## What to build
1. **UGBDataSubsystem**: load every file listed in the header comment from `FPaths::ProjectContentDir()/Data/` with `FFileHelper::LoadFileToString` + `FJsonSerializer` + `FJsonObjectConverter::JsonObjectToUStruct` / `JsonArrayToUStruct` (check their exact signatures in `Engine/Source/Runtime/JsonUtilities/Public/JsonObjectConverter.h`). Write ONE small generic helper for "load array field X of file F into TArray<T>" and one for "load whole file into struct T" and reuse them. Missing file or parse error: `UE_LOG(LogGB, Error, ...)` naming the file and the JSON error, plus an on-screen debug message in non-shipping builds, table left empty, no crash. Warn about duplicate ids and entries with an empty Id. `Find*` do a lookup through a TMap<FName,int32> index rebuilt on load (add the index maps as private members). `ReloadAll` re-reads everything, then broadcasts `OnDataReloaded`. `ParseColor` accepts "#RRGGBB" and "#RRGGBBAA" (sRGB hex to FLinearColor). `Get` returns the subsystem from the world's game instance (null-safe).
   - Console commands in `Glyphbound.cpp` using `FAutoConsoleCommandWithWorld` (or the WithWorldAndArgs variant): `gb.ReloadData` (calls ReloadAll on that world's game instance).
   - JSON keys must match the struct field names in `Data/GBDataTypes.h` (FJsonObjectConverter is case-insensitive on names; enums are written as their names, e.g. "Fire"; bools named `bEnabled` are written "bEnabled").
2. **FGBScaledParam::Resolve** per its header comment.
3. **UGBStatsComponent** per the header. `ApplyModifiers`: result = (Base + sum of Add) * product of Multiply; if any Override exists, the LAST Override wins and replaces the whole result. `Evaluate`/`EvaluateKeys` collect the active modifiers whose `Stat` equals one of the keys, in insertion order. `AddModifiers(Source, ...)` first removes that source, then adds each modifier with `Value` scaled by `ValueScale` this way: Add -> Value*Scale; Multiply -> 1 + (Value-1)*Scale; Override -> unchanged. Broadcast `OnStatsChanged` on any change. No tick.
4. **UGBAttributeComponent** per the header. Ticks to regenerate using `StepRegen` (no regen while dead; regen only after the delay since the last loss; clamp to max). When max health/mana drop below current values (stats changed), clamp. `ApplyDamage`: ignore if dead, invulnerable or Amount <= 0; copy the info, broadcast `OnModifyIncomingDamage(copy)`, multiply by the owner's `DamageTaken` stat (default 1), clamp to >= 0, subtract, broadcast `OnHealthChanged`, `OnDamaged(copy, actual)`, and on reaching 0 set dead and broadcast `OnDeath` once. `RestoreAll` revives. Bind to the owner's `UGBStatsComponent::OnStatsChanged` in BeginPlay to re-clamp and re-broadcast.
5. **GBPlaceholder** per the header. Meshes: `/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube.Cube`, `Sphere.Sphere`, `Cylinder.Cylinder`, `Cone.Cone`, `Plane.Plane` (all 100 cm). Materials: lit = `/Engine/BasicShapes/BasicShapeMaterial.BasicShapeMaterial` (vector parameter "Color"), glow = `/Engine/EngineMaterials/EmissiveMeshMaterial.EmissiveMeshMaterial` (vector parameter "Color", unlit additive). Load with `LoadObject` and cache in `TWeakObjectPtr` statics. `SetupShape` sets relative scale = SizeCm / 100, creates a `UMaterialInstanceDynamic` on slot 0 and sets "Color". `ElementColor(uint8)`: cast to `EGBElement` (Physical grey, Arcane violet, Fire orange, Lightning yellow, Ice cyan, Air pale green).
6. **UGBProgressSubsystem** per the header. `SaveCheckpoint` calls `AGBPlayerCharacter::SaveToSnapshot` and sets bValid; `RestoreCheckpoint` calls `LoadFromSnapshot` (the player header is `Player/GBPlayerCharacter.h`; you only call those two methods). Broadcast the delegates.
7. **StatusEffects.json**: `{ "StatusEffects": [ ... ] }` with these ids and provisional values: `Burn` (fire damage over time, 4 s, tick 0.5 s), `Shock` (short lightning effect: brief MoveSpeed x0.6 for 1.5 s), `Slow` (MoveSpeed x0.5, 4 s), `Chill` (MoveSpeed x0.7, 3 s), `HealthPotion` (heals over time: 10 s, tick 1 s, total about 60), `ManaPotion` (same idea for mana), `HealthInjection` (instant heal, smaller than the potion total, Duration 0), `Enchant_Fire`, `Enchant_Lightning`, `Enchant_Ice` (Duration 20 s; Modifiers on "Weapon.All.Damage" Multiply ~1.25; Strings: "WeaponElement": "Fire"/"Lightning"/"Ice" and "WeaponOnHitEffect": "Burn"/"Shock"/"Chill" - the gun code reads these two strings). Negative HealthPerTick = damage.
8. **Tests** (`Tests/GBStatsTests.cpp`), pure logic only, a handful: modifier order (add then multiply; last override wins; scaling of Multiply modifiers around 1), `StepRegen` (no regen before the delay, clamps at max, no regen at 0 rate), `FGBScaledParam::Resolve` (QTE off returns Base; Power-tagged ignores Reach; clamps scores to 0..1). Test names like `Glyphbound.Stats.ModifierOrder`.

Finish with the final report described in the rules file.

input.prompt:
You are implementer "COMBAT" on the Unreal Engine 5.9 C++ game Glyphbound. First read `C:\GameJam\Prompts\implementer_rules.md` and follow it exactly (it tells you what else to read). GDD sections for you: 3, 5, 6, 8, 10. Also read `Combat/GBStatusEffectComponent.h`, `Combat/GBProjectile.h`, `UI/GBPixelSpriteLibrary.h`, `AI/GBEnemyCharacter.h` (you call `IsHeadshotLocation` only if useful).

## Your files (you own only these; all under C:\GameJam\Glyphbound\Source\Glyphbound\)
- `Combat/GBCombatLibrary.cpp`, `Combat/GBStatusEffectComponent.cpp`, `Combat/GBProjectile.cpp` (new, for the three existing headers in `Combat/`)
- `Tests/GBCombatTests.cpp` (new)

## What to build
1. **UGBCombatLibrary** exactly per the header comments.
   - `DealDamage`: null-safe; target needs a `UGBAttributeComponent` (use `UGBAttributeComponent::Find`); skip if not hostile to the instigator unless `bAllowFriendlyFire` (a null instigator or a Neutral team always damages); multiply Amount by the instigator's `DamageDealt` stat if it has a `UGBStatsComponent` (default 1); call `ApplyDamage`; if the returned damage > 0 and `Info.OnHitEffect` is set and the target has a `UGBStatusEffectComponent`, call `ApplyEffect(OnHitEffect, Instigator, Info.EffectDurationScale, Info.EffectStrengthScale)`. Periodic damage from status effects must NOT re-apply on-hit effects (the effect component passes OnHitEffect = NAME_None).
   - `DealRadialDamage`: `UWorld::OverlapMultiByObjectType` with a sphere for Pawn + WorldDynamic object types, unique actors, skip `IgnoreActors`, skip actors without attributes, skip non-hostile to the instigator; per target fill HitLocation (target location) and HitDirection (from Origin); with falloff scale Amount by 1 - dist/Radius (clamped). Returns the count damaged.
   - Teams from `UGBAttributeComponent::Team`. `AreTeamsHostile`: Player vs Enemy only.
   - Pure math functions per their comments. `ApplySpread` uses `FMath::VRandCone`-style math with the given `FRandomStream` (check what the stream offers, e.g. `FRandomStream::VRandCone`).
2. **UGBStatusEffectComponent** per the header: definitions from `UGBDataSubsystem::FindStatusEffect` (looked up by id every time it is needed, never cached). On apply: instant health/mana (through the owner's `UGBAttributeComponent`: positive = Heal/RestoreMana, negative health = damage via `UGBCombatLibrary::DealDamage` with the effect's element, the stored instigator, SourceId = effect id, friendly fire allowed so a self-applied effect works), then if Duration*DurationScale > 0 it becomes active: modifiers added to the owner's `UGBStatsComponent` with a unique source name per active effect (e.g. "Effect.Slow#3") and `ValueScale = StrengthScale`. Re-apply: `bRefreshOnReapply` restarts the timer (and takes the larger strength); otherwise stack up to `MaxStacks` (each stack is its own entry). Tick: count down, run ticks every `TickInterval` (HealthPerTick/ManaPerTick scaled by StrengthScale), remove at the end (removing its modifier source). `OnEffectsChanged` on any add/remove. Effects stop ticking when the owner is dead and are all removed on death (bind to the attribute component's `OnDeath` in BeginPlay).
3. **AGBProjectile** per the header: `USphereComponent` root (collision: query only; overlap Pawn and WorldDynamic, block WorldStatic; `OnComponentHit` + `OnComponentBeginOverlap`), `UProjectileMovementComponent` (initial speed and max speed = Speed, gravity scale from config, `bShouldBounce` only when FuseTime > 0), a `UBillboardComponent` for pixel-art looks (set up through `UGBPixelSpriteLibrary::SetupBillboard(Sprite, Config.SpriteId, height = Radius*2*VisualScale)`) and a `UStaticMeshComponent` (no collision) for 3D looks (`GBPlaceholder::SetupShape` sphere, glow = true, Config.Color); show only the one that matches `bPixelArt`. `SpawnProjectile` spawns deferred (`SpawnActorDeferred`), calls `InitProjectile`, finishes spawning, and makes the projectile and its instigator ignore each other (`IgnoreActorWhenMoving` both ways).
   - On touching an actor: ignore the instigator, non-hostile actors with attributes, and other projectiles. Hostile actor with attributes: if `ExplosionRadius > 0` explode there, else `DealDamage` with a copy of `Config.Damage` (Causer = this, HitLocation = impact point, HitDirection = velocity direction) and set `bHeadshot` when the target is an `AGBEnemyCharacter` and `IsHeadshotLocation(impact)`; then finish unless `bPierce` (remember damaged actors so each is hit once).
   - On hitting the world: explode or finish (unless FuseTime > 0: keep bouncing).
   - `Tick`: finish (exploding if ExplosionRadius > 0) when travelled distance >= MaxRange (if > 0), lifetime > MaxLifetime, or the fuse runs out.
   - Explode = `UGBCombatLibrary::DealRadialDamage(Origin = location, ExplosionRadius, Damage, ignore = {}, bExplosionFalloff)`.
   - Finish = broadcast `OnImpact` once, then `Destroy()`.
4. **Tests** (`Tests/GBCombatTests.cpp`): `DistanceFalloffMultiplier` (near, far, midpoint, and FalloffEnd <= FalloffStart as a hard step), `IsHeadshot` (just above / just below the head line; HeadFraction 0 never a headshot), `AreTeamsHostile` (Player-Enemy both ways; Neutral with anyone false; same team false). Names like `Glyphbound.Combat.DistanceFalloff`.

Finish with the final report described in the rules file.

input.description: Implement player and input
input.prompt:
You are implementer "PLAYER" on the Unreal Engine 5.9 C++ game Glyphbound. First read `C:\GameJam\Prompts\implementer_rules.md` and follow it exactly (it tells you what else to read). GDD sections for you: 0, 3, 7 (the requirements about camera lock and movement during the QTE), 9 (the full control table), 10 ("Death and difficulty"). Also read every header in `Player/`, plus `Weapons/GBEquipmentComponent.h`, `Weapons/GBHeldItem.h`, `Spells/GBSpellbookComponent.h`, `QTE/GBQTEComponent.h`, `QTE/GBQTELogic.h`, `Items/GBInventoryComponent.h`, `Progression/GBSkillTreeComponent.h`, `World/GBInteractable.h`, `World/GBProgressSubsystem.h`, `World/GBEraSubsystem.h`, `Core/GBGameMode.h`, `UI/GBHUD.h`.

## Your files (you own only these; all under C:\GameJam\Glyphbound\)
- `Source/Glyphbound/Player/GBPlayerCharacter.cpp`, `Player/GBPlayerController.cpp`, `Player/GBInputSet.cpp` (new) and the three headers in `Player/` (you may add members; do not change existing public signatures)
- `Content/Data/Player.json` (new)

## What to build
1. **UGBInputSet::Build**: create every `UInputAction` (`NewObject<UInputAction>(this)`, set `ValueType`) and the two `UInputMappingContext`s, and map keys with `MapKey` (+ modifiers created with `NewObject`: `UInputModifierNegate`, `UInputModifierSwizzleAxis`, dead zones for sticks; check `Engine/Plugins/EnhancedInput/Source/EnhancedInput/Public`). Bindings: the whole table of GDD 9 for keyboard+mouse and gamepad. Notes:
   - Move: WASD + left stick (Axis2D, x = right, y = forward). Look: mouse XY + right stick (apply a per-second scale for the stick in the character, not here).
   - Add four extra button actions `QTEUp/QTELeft/QTEDown/QTERight` bound to W/A/S/D (a key may map to several actions); the gamepad uses the `Face*` actions.
   - `SwitchWeapon` (Axis1D): mouse wheel axis, Left Alt (+1), D-pad up (+1). `CycleQuickUse`: Left Shift (+1), D-pad right (+1) / left (-1).
   - Keyboard: Jump = Space, Dash = Left Ctrl, Primary = LMB, Secondary = RMB, SpellSlot1 = RMB, SpellSlot2-5 = 1,2,3,4, Enchant = T, Reload = R, Interact = G, QuickUse = F, Inventory = Tab, SkillTrees = K, Pause = Esc.
   - Gamepad: Primary = right trigger, Secondary = left trigger, SpellSlot1 = left shoulder, Enchant = left shoulder, QuickUse = right shoulder, Inventory = special left (View), Pause = special right (Menu); face buttons only through `Face*`.
   - MenuContext: navigate (arrows, WASD, D-pad, left stick), confirm (Enter, Space, gamepad face bottom), back (Esc, Tab, gamepad face right), tab (Q/E, shoulders).
2. **AGBPlayerCharacter** (first person): capsule + `UCameraComponent` at the `EyeHeight` stat, `bUsePawnControlRotation`, a `HeldItemAnchor` scene component under the camera (offset right/down/forward: a visual constant), all gameplay components created in the constructor with `CreateDefaultSubobject`. No mesh (hands are drawn by the HUD).
   - `BeginPlay` order: `Stats->SetBaseStats(Data->GetPlayer().Stats)`; `Attributes->Team = Player`; `Attributes->InitializeFromStats()`; give `Data->GetPlayer().StartingWeapons` through `Equipment->GiveWeapon(Id, bAutoSwitch = first one only, bDropOld = false)`; `Spellbook->InitializeFromData()`; `Inventory->InitializeFromData()`; `SkillTree->InitializeFromData()`; bind `Stats->OnStatsChanged` -> `ApplyMovementStats`; bind `Attributes->OnDeath` -> `HandleDeath`; bind `UGBDataSubsystem::OnDataReloaded` to re-set the base stats; finally, if `UGBProgressSubsystem` has no checkpoint, `SaveCheckpoint(this)`.
   - `ApplyMovementStats`: MaxWalkSpeed = MoveSpeed stat * MoveSpeedScale, JumpZVelocity, AirControl, GravityScale, `JumpMaxCount` = round(MaxJumps stat), capsule size, braking/acceleration tuned for a snappy shooter (visual-feel constants are fine).
   - Input: bind every action of the input set in `SetupPlayerInputComponent` (create `InputSet` there if null, call `Build()`, then `AGBPlayerController::SetupInput(InputSet)`). Rules:
     * If `!bControlEnabled` or dead: ignore gameplay input.
     * While `QTE->IsActive()`: Move and Look do not move or turn; the character keeps applying `LastMoveInput` as movement every tick; `QTEUp/Left/Down/Right` and `FaceUp/Left/Down/Right` call `QTE->HandleKey` (EGBQTEKey Up, Left, Down, Right); Look input goes to `QTE->HandleGestureInput` as a screen-space delta (x right, y DOWN: flip the mouse Y; for the stick multiply by delta time and a visual constant such as 900 px/s); every other gameplay action is ignored.
     * Otherwise: Primary -> active held item `StartPrimary`/`StopPrimary`. Secondary -> with a gun `StartSecondary`/`StopSecondary` (aim); with the staff nothing here (keyboard right click triggers `SpellSlot1`; on gamepad the left trigger is the spell modifier, see below). `SpellSlot1..5` -> `Spellbook->TryCastSlot(0..4)` only when holding the staff. `Enchant` -> `Spellbook->TryCastEnchant()` only when holding a gun (so left shoulder = slot 1 with the staff and enchant with a gun, with no clash). `Reload`, `Interact` (calls `Interact(this)` on the focused interactable if `CanInteract`), `QuickUse` -> `Inventory->UseQuickItem()`, `CycleQuickUse`, `SwitchWeapon` -> `Equipment->CycleSlot(sign)` (ignore tiny axis noise; one step per press).
     * Gamepad face buttons outside the QTE: with the staff in hand and the left trigger held, FaceDown/FaceRight/FaceLeft/FaceUp cast spell slots 2,3,4,5 (GDD 9: L2 + Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle); otherwise FaceDown = jump, FaceRight = dash, FaceLeft = reload, FaceUp = interact.
   - Jump: `Jump()` / `StopJumping()` (double jump comes from JumpMaxCount). Dash: if the cooldown is ready, direction = current movement input in world space (forward if none), horizontal only; for `DashDuration` seconds move at `DashDistance / DashDuration` speed (set the velocity each tick, zero gravity effect on Z during the dash is fine), then restore; cooldown `DashCooldown` starts at the dash start. Allowed in the air. No invulnerability (provisional).
   - `AddRecoil`: add to control rotation immediately (pitch up), remember it in `PendingRecoil`, and recover towards zero in Tick at the given speed.
   - `UpdateFocusedInteractable` every tick: sphere-overlap (default channels: WorldDynamic + WorldStatic + Pawn object types) around the camera within the `InteractRange` stat, keep actors implementing `UGBInteractable` whose `CanInteract(this)` is true, prefer the one closest to the view direction (dot product), require a rough facing (dot > 0.3).
   - `GetMuzzleLocation`: camera location + a small forward/right/down offset. `RestoreAll`: `Attributes->RestoreAll()` + `Equipment->RefillAllAmmo()`.
   - `HandleDeath`: `SetControlEnabled(false)`, `Spellbook->CancelSustained()`, `QTE->CancelQTE()`, then `AGBGameMode::Get(this)->HandlePlayerDeath(this)`.
   - `SaveToSnapshot` / `LoadFromSnapshot`: transform, control rotation, era (`UGBEraSubsystem::GetCurrentEra` / `SetEraImmediate`), health and mana (`SetHealthAndMana`; call `Attributes->RestoreAll()` first to revive), then each component's own Save/Load. On load also zero the velocity, end any dash and `SetControlEnabled(true)`.
   - `static Get`: the pawn of the first local player controller, cast.
3. **AGBPlayerController**: `SetupInput` stores the set, adds `GameplayContext` to the `UEnhancedInputLocalPlayerSubsystem`, and binds Inventory / SkillTrees / Pause and the menu actions on its own `UEnhancedInputComponent` (the controller's `InputComponent`). `SetMenu(Menu)`: for Pause, Inventory, SkillTrees: `SetPause(true)`, remove the gameplay context, add the menu context, show the mouse cursor is NOT needed (keyboard/gamepad navigation only), notify `AGBHUD::OnMenuOpened`. For Death: no pause, add the menu context, notify the HUD. For None: unpause, restore contexts, `OnMenuClosed`. Menu actions must still trigger while paused (set `bTriggerWhenPaused = true` on those `UInputAction`s in the input set). Pause key: toggles Pause, or closes whatever menu is open. Tab / K toggle Inventory / SkillTrees. Menu navigate: convert the Axis2D value to an `FIntPoint` step (x right, y down), one step per press (use the Started trigger event). `MenuConfirm` -> HUD, except in the Death menu where it calls `AGBGameMode::RespawnPlayer()`. `MenuBack` -> if the HUD's `MenuBack()` returns false, close the menu (not for Death). `MenuTab` -> HUD.
4. **Player.json** (`FGBPlayerDefinition`, one object): provisional values for a fast shooter: MaxHealth 100, HealthRegen 2, HealthRegenDelay 5, MaxMana 100, ManaRegen 6, ManaRegenDelay 1.5, MoveSpeed 750, JumpVelocity 620, MaxJumps 1, AirControl 0.6, GravityScale 1.6, DashDistance 700, DashDuration 0.18, DashCooldown 1.2, InteractRange 250, DamageTaken 1, DamageDealt 1, CapsuleRadius 38, CapsuleHalfHeight 90, EyeHeight 70. `StartingWeapons`: ["Staff_Apprentice"]. `StartingSpells`: ["Air_DoubleJump"] (provisional, so double jump can be tested on day 1; MaxJumps base stays 1 and the passive adds 1). `StartingLoadout`: ["Fireball", "LightningBolt", "IceWall"]. `StartingItems`: {"HealthPotion": 2, "ManaPotion": 2}. `StartingSkillPoints`: 2. `EnchantSpell`: "WeaponEnchant". `StartingEnchantElement`: "Fire".

Finish with the final report described in the rules file.

   - Gamepad: Primary = right trigger, Secondary = left trigger, SpellSlot1 = left shoulder, Enchant = left shoulder, QuickUse = right shoulder, Inventory = special left (View), Pause = special right (Menu); face buttons only through `Face*`.
   - MenuContext: navigate (arrows, WASD, D-pad, left stick), confirm (Enter, Space, gamepad face bottom), back (Esc, Tab, gamepad face right), tab (Q/E, shoulders).
2. **AGBPlayerCharacter** (first person): capsule + `UCameraComponent` at the `EyeHeight` stat, `bUsePawnControlRotation`, a `HeldItemAnchor` scene component under the camera (offset right/down/forward: a visual constant), all gameplay components created in the constructor with `CreateDefaultSubobject`. No mesh (hands are drawn by the HUD).
   - `BeginPlay` order: `Stats->SetBaseStats(Data->GetPlayer().Stats)`; `Attributes->Team = Player`; `Attributes->InitializeFromStats()`; give `Data->GetPlayer().StartingWeapons` through `Equipment->GiveWeapon(Id, bAutoSwitch = first one only, bDropOld = false)`; `Spellbook->InitializeFromData()`; `Inventory->InitializeFromData()`; `SkillTree->InitializeFromData()`; bind `Stats->OnStatsChanged` -> `ApplyMovementStats`; bind `Attributes->OnDeath` -> `HandleDeath`; bind `UGBDataSubsystem::OnDataReloaded` to re-set the base stats; finally, if `UGBProgressSubsystem` has no checkpoint, `SaveCheckpoint(this)`.
   - `ApplyMovementStats`: MaxWalkSpeed = MoveSpeed stat * MoveSpeedScale, JumpZVelocity, AirControl, GravityScale, `JumpMaxCount` = round(MaxJumps stat), capsule size, braking/acceleration tuned for a snappy shooter (visual-feel constants are fine).
   - Input: bind every action of the input set in `SetupPlayerInputComponent` (create `InputSet` there if null, call `Build()`, then `AGBPlayerController::SetupInput(InputSet)`). Rules:
     * If `!bControlEnabled` or dead: ignore gameplay input.
     * While `QTE->IsActive()`: Move and Look do not move or turn; the character keeps applying `LastMoveInput` as movement every tick; `QTEUp/Left/Down/Right` and `FaceUp/Left/Down/Right` call `QTE->HandleKey` (EGBQTEKey Up, Left, Down, Right); Look input goes to `QTE->HandleGestureInput` as a screen-space delta (x right, y DOWN: flip the mouse Y; for the stick multiply by delta time and a visual constant such as 900 px/s); every other gameplay action is ignored.
     * Otherwise: Primary -> active held item `StartPrimary`/`StopPrimary`. Secondary -> with a gun `StartSecondary`/`StopSecondary` (aim); with the staff nothing here (keyboard right click triggers `SpellSlot1`; on gamepad the left trigger is the spell modifier, see below). `SpellSlot1..5` -> `Spellbook->TryCastSlot(0..4)` only when holding the staff. `Enchant` -> `Spellbook->TryCastEnchant()` only when holding a gun (so left shoulder = slot 1 with the staff and enchant with a gun, with no clash). `Reload`, `Interact` (calls `Interact(this)` on the focused interactable if `CanInteract`), `QuickUse` -> `Inventory->UseQuickItem()`, `CycleQuickUse`, `SwitchWeapon` -> `Equipment->CycleSlot(sign)` (ignore tiny axis noise; one step per press).
     * Gamepad face buttons outside the QTE: with the staff in hand and the left trigger held, FaceDown/FaceRight/FaceLeft/FaceUp cast spell slots 2,3,4,5 (GDD 9: L2 + Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle); otherwise FaceDown = jump, FaceRight = dash, FaceLeft = reload, FaceUp = interact.
   - Jump: `Jump()` / `StopJumping()` (double jump comes from JumpMaxCount).    - `AddRecoil`: add to control rotation immediately (pitch up), remember it in `PendingRecoil`, and recover towards zero in Tick at the given speed.
   - `UpdateFocusedInteractable` every tick: sphere-overlap (default channels: WorldDynamic + WorldStatic + Pawn object types) around the camera within the `InteractRange` stat, keep actors implementing `UGBInteractable` whose `CanInteract(this)` is true, prefer the one closest to the view direction (dot product), require a rough facing (dot > 0.3).
   - `GetMuzzleLocation`: camera location + a small forward/right/down offset. `RestoreAll`: `Attributes->RestoreAll()` + `Equipment->RefillAllAmmo()`.
   - `HandleDeath`: `SetControlEnabled(false)`, `Spellbook->CancelSustained()`, `QTE->CancelQTE()`, then `AGBGameMode::Get(this)->HandlePlayerDeath(this)`.

Menu actions must still trigger while paused (set `bTriggerWhenPaused = true` on those `UInputAction`s in the input set). Pause key: toggles Pause, or closes whatever menu is open. Tab / K toggle Inventory / SkillTrees.
